## PPC fast Java bundle setup

PPC `NSJavaBundleSetup` dispatches to the reconstructed
`__NSFastJavaBundleSetup` path only when `_usesFastJavaBundleSetup` is positive.
The fast path aggregates framework paths before bundle paths, registers the
setup dictionary's native library paths once, and marks and loads each
Java-providing bundle before loading requested classes. The DR2 i386 image has
no corresponding export and continues through the existing non-fast setup
path. Its PPC `NSJavaSetupVirtualMachine` wrapper sets `NSJavaNeeded` to
`@"YES"` before delegating to `NSJavaSetup`, as in the target.

The non-fast setup path preserves its target-specific bundle load order: PPC
adds `allFrameworks` before `allBundles`, while i386 uses the reverse order.
`NSJavaSetup.m` now selects the sequence by architecture, matching
`_NSJavaBundleSetup` at PPC `0x4257bb14` and i386 `0x425554a0`.

The PPC non-fast path also posts the four VM setup notifications in target
order: will-setup before VM bundle resolution, will-create before VM
initialization, did-create immediately after initialization, and did-setup
after configured classes load. The i386 path has no corresponding posts. This
PPC-only sequence is now guarded in `NSJavaSetup.m`.

## `NSDictionary` concrete retain locks

MOSXS PPC `NSConcreteDictionary` and `NSConcreteMutableDictionary` use the
`___NSDictionaryRetainLock` spin word for inline retain-count updates when
`_NSIsMultiThreaded` is true. Their retain and release paths saturate at
`UINT_MAX`, emit allocation-statistics events around the count change, and
deallocate after releasing the lock when the stored count was zero. Their
`retainCount` methods return the stored count plus one. DR2 i386 continues to
use `_NSGlobalRetainLock` through the shared internal refcount helpers. The PPC
lock export is recorded in `abi-ppc/NSDictionary.json`.

the class-side `debugDescription` already recorded in the shared ABI, and the

PPC stores `___NSSequenceLock` as a zero-initialized spin word and uses

## i386/PPC uncaught exception stack reporting

Both `_NSRaiseError` bodies call the installed uncaught-exception handler,
format a stack with `NSStringFromStack(@"0x%x", @" ")`, and log the exception
name, reason, and stack using
`*** Uncaught exception: <%@> %@\nstack: %@\n`. `NSException.m` now follows
that reporting path on both targets; the frame walker remains implemented in
`NSDebug.m`. The `NSHangOnUncaughtException` suspend and exit behavior is
unchanged. This adds no ABI entries. The format strings and call order were
confirmed in the i386 and PPC `_NSRaiseError` disassembly.

The uncaught-report argument evaluation order differs by target. i386 captures
the stack before querying the exception reason and name; PPC queries name and
reason before capturing the stack. `NSException.m` now preserves that ordering
under the target compiler guards while passing name, reason, and stack to
`NSLog` in the same format order on both targets.

## i386/PPC per-thread assertion handlers

Both `+[NSAssertionHandler currentHandler]` bodies use the current thread's
`threadDictionary` under the `NSAssertionHandler` key. On a miss they allocate
and initialize a base `NSAssertionHandler`, store it in that dictionary, then
release the temporary ownership. `NSException.m` now follows this path instead
of sharing one process-global handler. The key, class receiver, dictionary
operations, and release are confirmed in both IDA targets. No ABI entries
changed.

## i386/PPC assertion failure reports

Both `handleFailureInMethod:...` implementations call `_NSFullMethodName`
with the object and selector, then log the method name, source file, and line
using `*** Assertion failure in %@, %@:%d`. The selector is a legacy
`SEL` backed by the selector-name C string, matching `_NSFullMethodName`'s
`char *` argument. Both `handleFailureInFunction:...` implementations log
`*** Assertion failure in %@(), %@:%d` before raising
`NSInternalInconsistencyException` with the original format and `va_list`.
`NSException.m` now follows those report paths. The two format strings and
helper calls were checked in the i386 and PPC IDA databases; no ABI entries
changed.

The paired addresses and source audit are recorded in
`docs/superpowers/plans/notes/2026-10-03-foundation-nspathstore2-analysis.md`.
No ABI entries changed; tests and builds were not run.

`_NSStandardizePath` also uses the reference's 1,024-unit stack scratch area

## `NSDecimalRound` sign-dependent rounding (closed, 2026-10-06)

`NSDecimalRound` uses sign-specific rounding dispatch in i386
`0x425a119c` and PPC `0x4255c52c`. The PPC body confirms that `NSRoundDown`
increments the magnitude only for negative values, while `NSRoundUp` does so
only for positive values; plain rounding uses the discarded digit, and
banker's ties use opposite retained-digit parity for negative values. The
negative banker’s tie branch therefore increments when the retained mantissa
is even, matching the target behavior. `NSDecimal.m` now uses a
`NSDecimalRound`-local helper for those rules; `ShouldRoundUp` remains
sign-independent for `NSDecimalAdd` and `NSDecimalMultiply`, whose
`RoundToFit` paths use it. No ABI entries changed; no tests or builds were
run.

increment the retained value. `ShouldRoundUp` previously treated its default
case as `NSRoundPlain`, so `NSDecimalAdd` and `NSDecimalMultiply` could
increment for invalid modes. Its default now skips the increment; all four

## `NSSerialization` target byte and bitfield order (closed, 2026-10-06)

The compact integer stream is little-endian on both targets. i386 reads and
writes its native integer bytes in stream order; PPC reverses its native
big-endian bytes when encoding and decoding. The serializer now normalizes
PPC integers to the same little-endian stream before applying the compact
length marker. The type-walker bitfield helpers also follow the target layout:
i386 maps fields least-significant-bit first, while PPC maps fields
most-significant-bit first. These shared helpers serve both property-list and
type-walker serialization paths. The existing bitfield width guard and ABI
records are unchanged. The implementation was checked statically; tests and
builds were not run.

## `NSInvocation` distributed-object coder wire (closed, 2026-10-07)

Both targets encode the invocation header as target (`@`), argument count
(`I`), selector (`:`), method type string (`*`), and return-value tag
(`i`). Arguments from index 2 use their signature type encodings; pointer
arguments carry a `c` null flag and, when non-null, the pointee value. Decode
validates the target's method signature against the wire signature by identity
and keeps the decoded signature available for argument records. Pointer
backing bytes are retained through the invocation's container.

i386 decodes ordinary arguments directly into their frame offsets and applies
`_NSParseAndAutorelease` to decoded pointer pointees. PPC decodes through
aligned stack temporary storage, applies the record/frame
`autorelease_pointers` walk, and copies pointer/value slots through
`setArgument:atIndex:`. On i386, a non-null pointer slot is written directly
to its measured frame offset before decoding the pointee; the null flag leaves
the zero-initialized slot unchanged. PPC's pointer slot remains live through
its setter.
PPC does not additionally call `_NSParseAndAutorelease`; that parser helper
remains on the i386 path. The 36-byte instance layout and ABI records are
unchanged. Static source and selector checks were used; no tests or builds
were run.

Mapped PPC `_autorelease_pointers` (`0x4258683c`, 172 bytes) to the recursive
`NSInvocationAutoreleasePointers` helper in `NSInvocation.m`. It skips type
qualifiers, autoreleases object slots, skips character pointers, and descends
the nested argument records for aggregate values. The PPC invocation-coding
source map now includes this helper entry.

### `_preInitWithCoder:` target signature ownership correction (2026-10-08)

Both i386 (`0x42551260`) and PPC (`0x4253bc3c`) retain the target's method
signature before comparing it with the decoded wire signature. On a match,
that retained reference becomes the invocation signature; on a mismatch, the
target signature is released and the decoded signature is retained instead.
The source previously released the borrowed target signature on mismatch.
`NSInvocation.m` now retains it before the comparison and transfers that
reference on the match path, balancing both target branches. Static
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

The same mismatch branch logs the selector name, decoded signature, and
target signature with `%s incompatible method params: got %@ want %@\n` on
both targets (i386 `0x42551260`, PPC `0x4253bc3c`). The source now uses
`sel_getName(_cmd)` and the target format and argument order.

Both `_postInitWithCoder:...` bodies decode the return tag before allocating
struct-return storage, and allocate only when that decoded tag is the struct
tag. They size and zero the buffer from the wire signature (i386
`0x42549a80`, PPC `0x4253c678`). The source now follows this order, instead of
initializing the return tag and buffer from the selected signature before
decoding the wire tag.

For decoded non-null pointer arguments, i386 `_postInitWithCoder:...` rejects
a zero-sized pointee with `NSInternalInconsistencyException` and
`bad size for type %s\n` (`0x42549a80`). PPC (`0x4253c678`) has no such check
and passes the size to `NSMutableData -initWithLength:`. The source now guards
the check to i386 and matches its exception name and text.

Both `newInvocationWithCoder:` factories install the inline frame pointer
only when `NSAllocateObject` succeeds, then send `_postInitWithCoder:...` to
the result either way (i386 `0x425511c8`, PPC `0x4253b844`). A nil result
therefore returns nil through ordinary nil-message dispatch without releasing
the retained signature. The source now follows that path rather than adding
an allocation-failure release and early return.

Both `_postInitWithCoder:...` bodies install the selector at argument index 1
before the target at index 0 (i386 `0x42549a80`, PPC `0x4253c678`). The source
now preserves that send order before enabling retained-argument handling.

The i386 encoder at `0x4252b37c` raises

guard, and the return-value coder helper does not use it. The shared encoder
helper now performs the check only for i386 `encodeWithCoder:` calls. Static
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

The DR2 i386 method (`0x4257f168`) writes the data to a globally unique

the source now preserves that predicate instead of checking only for a
negative result.

stores both conversion results in order, while retaining the target's
conditional destination-existence check and error path. Static paired

The i386 `_NSReadBytesFromFile` has four arguments and returns a static
zero-length buffer for empty files. Its `_NSMapBytesFromFile` uses `map_fd`,
and `-[NSData initWithContentsOfMappedFile:]` initializes VM-backed data from
that mapping. PPC `_NSReadBytesFromFile` has a fifth `allocatePages` argument;
its true branch allocates with `NSAllocateMemoryPages`, and PPC
`_NSMapBytesFromFile` calls that branch. PPC
`-[NSData initWithContentsOfMappedFile:]` forwards to
`initWithContentsOfFile:` instead. The source now uses the per-architecture
reader signatures, allocator/free paths, and initializer behavior. No symbol
assignments changed; no tests or builds were run.

On PPC, `-[NSConcreteData initWithBytes:length:copy:freeWhenDone:bytesAreVM:]`
also frees a non-null input on its zero-length path when `freeWhenDone` is true;
i386 does not. The source preserves this ownership difference so the empty-file
buffer from the PPC shared reader is released.

## `NSInvocation` argument frames and retained arguments (2026-10-07)

PPC `NSMethodSignature` records describe register, floating-register, and stack
locations, with nested aggregate records used to map packed struct bytes to the
call frame. `NSInvocation` now scatters and gathers struct fields through those
records and widens/narrows floating arguments when the frame slot is wider than
the declared value. Retained-argument walks use the signature records on PPC;
i386 continues to use `_NSParseAndRetain` and `_NSParseAndRelease`. The coder
temporarily disables retained-argument handling while restoring decoded
arguments, then restores the flag. Target and selector accessors route through
the argument get/set methods. These changes preserve the existing ivar layout
and selector ABI. The later `NSInvocation` object-layout ABI follow-up closes
the static layout concern; runtime behavior remains unverified. Static
source/IDA review only; tests/builds were not run.

source wrappers previously performed separate element-by-element loops; they

removals. No ABI records changed. Static IDA/source review only; tests and

The no-range `removeObject:` and `removeObjectIdenticalTo:` methods also

read the low 27-bit count directly for exact concrete arrays and use `count`
for other implementations. The source now preserves that class-dependent
count path instead of routing through the range wrapper.

## `NSMutableArray removeLastObject` and `removeAllObjects` (2026-10-07)

## `NSSet` base collection operations (2026-10-07)

The `NSCountedSet` initializer wrappers `initWithArray:` and `initWithSet:`

## Simple dictionary count-removal primitives (2026-10-07)

Paired DR2 i386 and MOSXS PPC IDA review found `NSSimpleDictionaryDecrementValue`
(i386 `0x42563364`, PPC `0x4256d94c`) masks the hash to 30 bits, finds the
matching bucket, decrements its stored integer value, and returns zero while
that value remains nonzero. On transition to zero it writes the stored key
through `keyPointer`, marks the bucket deleted, clears its key/value, decrements
the table count, and returns one. The source delegates lookup and removal to
helpers with the same hash-mask and bucket-removal behavior.

The paired `NSSimpleDictionaryDeleteEntriesWithValue` bodies (i386
`0x42563400`, PPC `0x4256da30`) scan buckets in descending index order, remove
occupied entries whose stored value matches, compact low-level tables by moving
the last counted bucket into the removed slot, preserve the level bits while
updating the count, and resize only when the level capacity is below the final
count. Return values differ by target: i386 returns the capacity-table address
when no resize occurs and the table pointer for an initially empty table; PPC
returns the remaining count, including zero for an initially empty table.
`NSSimpleHashing.m` now preserves that split. `NSResetSimpleDictionary` and
`NSResetSimpleSet` (i386 `0x4250328c`, `0x42517fe0`; PPC `0x425110e8`,
`0x4253c158`) likewise return target-specific initial values and callback
results; their source paths now match the paired IDA bodies.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.
The paired `NSSimpleDictionaryDelete` bodies (i386 `0x4250df5c`, PPC
`0x425093dc`) return the stored key and value before applying the same
low-level compaction or tombstone removal. The paired
`NSSimpleDictionaryIncrementValue` bodies (i386 `0x425634e4`, PPC
`0x4256db74`) increment an existing stored value and return its canonical key;
for a miss they insert the masked hash, original key, and value one, saturate
the count at `0x07ffffff`, and resize when the current level capacity is
exceeded. The implementations in `NSSimpleHashing.m` follow these paths.
Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or builds were run.

## Simple dictionary bucket-search parity (2026-10-07)

The paired `_NSSimpleDictionaryFindBuckets` bodies (i386 `0x42503550`, PPC
`0x42501098`) match the source's two storage modes. Dense level-0/1 tables
compare pointer identity first (i386 ascending, PPC descending), then run the
hash-filtered equality callback scan in ascending order. Larger tables use the
same hash-derived start and probe step, stop at a never-used slot, remember the
first tombstone for insertion, and compare stored hashes before calling the
equality callback. `NSSimpleHashing.m` preserves the target-specific dense scan
order and shared tombstone/probe behavior.

Paired `_NSSimpleDictFindBucketMatch` bodies (i386 `0x42503024`, PPC
`0x42500cbc`) use the same identity, hash, equality-callback, and probe rules
for lookup. `NSSimpleDictionaryLookup` delegates to the shared search routine
and returns its match. Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or builds were
run.
## Simple dictionary insertion parity (2026-10-07)

The paired `NSSimpleDictionaryInsert` bodies (i386 `0x425032fc`, PPC
`0x42501324`) use the shared bucket finder. On a match they optionally replace
the stored value, return the previous value through `valuePointer`, and return
the canonical stored key through `keyPointer`. On a miss they insert the masked
hash with the supplied key/value, saturate the count at `0x07ffffff`, and
resize when the capacity for the current level is exceeded. `NSSimpleHashing.m`
implements the same hit/miss ownership and resizing flow. Static paired
IDA/source review; no tests or builds were run.

## Simple dictionary resize parity (2026-10-07)

The paired `_NSResizeSimpleDictionary` bodies (i386 `0x425065f0`, PPC
`0x42526440`) allocate the replacement table in the old table's zone using its
count and equality callback, then traverse old buckets from highest index to
lowest and copy occupied entries. For level-0/1 replacement tables they append
densely in that traversal order; for larger tables they reinsert by masked hash
using the no-match probe helper. Both preserve `retainCount`, rebuild the count
and level bits from copied entries, free the old table, and return the new one.
`NSSimpleHashing.m` follows this allocation, copy, metadata, and ownership
sequence. Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or builds were run.

## Simple set search and resize parity (2026-10-07)

table. The source follows the same flow. Static paired IDA/source review; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSFileHandle` async-state allocation fields

DR2 i386 `_NSHiddenDataAllocate` (`0x42584fe0`) allocates 40 bytes with a
reserved word after the mutex. MOSXS PPC (`0x4259c2c4`) allocates 36 bytes and
omits that word. The source now keeps the reserved field only on i386, matching
the target offsets used by `performFunction:`, the workers, and
`handleMachMessage:` on each architecture.

Both allocators initialize the lock, reference count, port, error, data pointer,
and accepted descriptor; they leave the descriptor, native handle, and result
length untouched. The source matches those writes, with `performFunction:`
setting the descriptor and native handle before starting a worker and each
worker setting the result fields it reads. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

The PPC `_NSHiddenDataReleaseDidDeallocate` body acquires the embedded lock
with an atomic retry loop, yields after each busy result, issues `isync` after
acquisition, and issues `sync` before clearing the lock. The i386 body calls
`mutex_try_lock` and falls back to `mutex_wait_lock`. `NSFileHandle.m` now
keeps that i386 path and uses a PPC retry/yield loop with the matching acquire
and release barriers. The refcount decrement, unlock, and final deallocation
order match both IDA bodies. No tests or builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` positive mapped-data path (superseded)

For positive powers above 76, the target reads reduced-index divisor rows
from image-adjacent data and ignores the multiplication status, including
unchecked writes beyond the declared destination capacity. `NSDecimal.m` now
reproduces those rows from architecture-specific IDA snapshots and sparse
records through power 26,401, with a preflight that requires every lookup to
have its full divisor span captured or to follow a zero intermediate. This
supersedes the earlier 77-through-255 count-only implementation. At this
stage, positive direct calls above 26,401 remained outside the mapped source
tables; the complete signed-short image reconstruction below closes that gap
for both signs. No ABI entries changed; no tests or builds were run.

is 32 at index 62; its 32 divisor words are now represented in
`NSDecimal.m`. The next i386 count is 184, and PPC has no out-of-table count
that fits within 48 words. The source now follows the reference's compare and
divide behavior for negative powers through -255 when the source mantissa is
at most 48 words. At that stage, direct negative calls beyond that source
length or power range remained open; the complete signed-short image
reconstruction below closes those gaps. No ABI entries changed; no tests or
builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` negative range through mapped image data (superseded)

The preceding negative direct-source entry is superseded for source mantissas

reduced indices 39 through 26,363; architecture-specific bitmaps and sorted
small-divisor tables now model them in `NSDecimal.m`. Negative powers through
-26,401 use the reference's zero-count, length-only compare, and divisor paths
when the required data is represented. i386's captured raw prefix supplies
additional complete divisor spans, with the bitmap and sparse records
covering the remaining short cases. It has no IDA value at index 26,364,
which set the mapped-range boundary at that stage. The complete signed-short

Update (2026-10-08): `NSIntegerDivide` now uses the paired dynamic
work-array algorithm, so its prior 48-word reconstruction limit no longer
applies. Both architectures share a mapped-negative-power preflight: complete

unretained counts are accepted only when their known greater-than-48 length
forces the target's initial length comparison to clear the quotient. The final
remainder divide supports powers through 38. Unrepresented rows still use the
bounded fallback. The positive image-tail multiply path is extended by the
exact-span and zero-count selection below; direct-call powers not admitted by
that preflight remain on the bounded path. No ABI entries changed; no tests or
builds were run.

The earlier positive zero-count entry is superseded for powers 77 through

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` positive exact-span selection

The contiguous exact ranges remain original powers through 19,639 on i386 and
19,490 on PPC. The i386 raw snapshot includes initialized bytes through the
first unmapped address. Later reduced indices are read from that prefix only
when their complete divisor span fits; the IDA-derived bitmaps and sparse
records supply additional exact zero or short-divisor cases. IDA confirms

is zero and returns before reading divisor words. The i386 preflight therefore
requires complete spans only until the first zero-count intermediate; later
loop steps still require their count slots, all of which are captured through
reduced index 26,363. This admits 4,028 additional original powers from 19,640
through 26,401 whose lookup and multiply paths are represented, including
1,358 powers above 23,409. Powers with an unavailable nonzero span before a
zero-count intermediate stay on the bounded path. PPC's contiguous raw span
ends at original power 19,490, but the mapped-row preflight below also admits
later powers through 26,401 when each required nonzero divisor is retained or
an earlier zero has made divisor reads unreachable. Update (2026-10-08):
negative direct calls use the normalized dynamic divider on both targets and
the shared mapped-row preflight described above; the former i386-only
large-source restriction and 48-word divider limit are superseded. No ABI
entries changed; no tests or builds were run.

## Run-loop activity monitor lifecycle

Paired IDA review of `-[NSRunLoop addRunLoopActivityMonitor:]` (i386
`0x4253450c`, PPC `0x42536114`), `_informMonitors` (i386 `0x4250e6c0`, PPC
`0x42511b10`), and `acceptInputForMode:beforeDate:` (i386 `0x42510f98`, PPC
`0x42516180`) matches `NSRunLoop.m`. The first monitor is retained separately;
later monitors are retained in an ordered vector and notified in reverse
order. On a reclaiming callback with `quit` set, the run loop calls
`monitoringDiscontinued` before releasing/removing that monitor, then frees an
empty vector. Idle activity is reported before waiting when monitors may post
idle work, and handled-message activity follows dispatch. No source correction
was indicated. Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteTimer` retain, release, and fire paths

Paired DR2 i386 and MOSXS PPC IDA review confirms the two allocation events in
`NSConcreteTimer -retain` and `-release` are intentional. Each target method
records one event directly and its internal refcount helper records the other
(i386 helpers `0x4250b348` / `0x42506554`; PPC helpers `0x42532654` /
`0x4251a8f8`). The source's two explicit event calls preserve that total and
order; saturated counts additionally use the extra-refcount helper's event.
The packed state layout differs by target: i386 stores flags in bits 0–7 and
the 24-bit reference count in bits 8–31; PPC stores the reference count in bits
0–23 and uses bits 28–31 for user-info argument, repeats, invalid, and firing
flags respectively. `NSTimer.m` now selects the target masks and count shift,
so `init`, retain/release/count, equality, validity, invalidation, description,
and firing all read the matching layout. The paired `-fire` bodies confirm
reentrant or invalid timers return, target invocation is exception-isolated,
repeating timers advance from the prior fire date and clamp to current time,
and nonrepeating or invalidated timers invalidate. Their repeat-fire clamp
also differs for unordered values: PPC `fcmpu`/`bge` (`0x425446f8`) selects the
current time when the comparison is unordered, while i386's x87 less-than test
(`0x4251e6c8`) preserves an unordered next-fire time. `NSTimer.m` now keeps
that target-specific comparison. Static paired IDA/source review; no tests or
builds were run.

The replacement-date allocation call also differs: i386 (`0x4251e6c8`) and
PPC (`0x425446f8`) send `allocWithZone:nil` to `NSDate` before
`initWithTimeIntervalSinceReferenceDate:`. `NSTimer.m` now sends
`allocWithZone:NULL` at that site, which supplies the target's nil zone. Static
paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

Paired IDA review of delayed performers found `NSRunLoopPerformer`'s local
overlay omitted the object's `isa` word and represented the state bitfields
as a byte plus padding. The target layout is `isa`, link, target, selector,
argument, order, modes, then the `firing`/`invalid`/reference-count bitfields.
This shifted the source's link and order reads and made the invalid/firing
masks wrong on PPC. The overlay now mirrors `NSPerformTimerPrivate.h`'s field
layout and `_doPerformersForMode:reclaim:` / `cancelPerformSelector:` read the
bitfields directly, letting each target ABI supply its bit ordering. Evidence:
i386 `performSelector:target:argument:order:modes:` `0x4251813c`,
`_doPerformersForMode:reclaim:` `0x4250cf20`, `invalidate` `0x4250bc34`,
`fire` `0x425124f0`; PPC `performSelector:target:argument:order:modes:`
`0x4251d9a0`, `_doPerformersForMode:reclaim:` `0x42516f00`, `invalidate`
`0x42518aa0`, `fire` `0x4251fcd0`. Both `_doPerformersForMode:reclaim:` bodies first walk the full list and fire non-invalid performers whose mode list contains the requested mode. When `reclaim` is true, they then unlink and release invalid nodes from the head and interior of the list; when false, they skip reclamation. The source matches this traversal and release order. The paired run-loop maps record 222 i386 bytes and 280 PPC bytes at source line 864. No ABI entries changed; static paired
IDA/source review only, no tests or builds were run.

Paired IDA review of `_nextTimerInterval:forMode:modeInfo:` (i386

Both targets reuse a flagged future deadline, clear an expired cached flag, scan timer/mode pairs, remove invalid timers in place, and test mode membership. They read the current time lazily, cache the earliest future matching fire date, or retain/remove/fire a due timer and reinsert it only if it remains valid. If any timer fired, both then process performers and notify run-loop monitors before returning the cached deadline and flag. The source follows the same scan, ownership, and callback order. No ABI
entries changed; static paired IDA/source review only, no tests or builds were
run.

Paired IDA review of `allModes` (i386 `0x4258198c`, PPC `0x42597260`) and

## `NSDecimalNumberHandler` rounding and error policy

Paired IDA review confirms `initWithRoundingMode:scale:raiseOnExactness:raiseOnOverflow:raiseOnUnderflow:raiseOnDivideByZero:` stores the four raise flags in the target bitfield, and `roundingMode`/`scale` return their stored values (i386 initializer `0x4259c5fc`, PPC `0x4255cd1c`). PPC `-[NSDecimalNumberHandler exceptionDuringOperation:error:leftOperand:rightOperand:]` maps the underflow and overflow errors to their matching flags and exception names (`0x425c012c`). The i386 body (`0x4259c4f0`) instead pairs the underflow error value with the underflow flag but raises the overflow exception, and pairs the overflow error value with the overflow flag but raises the underflow exception. The source now preserves this i386 name/format swap and the PPC mapping. The default-handler singleton uses plain rounding, no scale, and raises for overflow, underflow, and divide-by-zero.

Paired IDA review of the string constructors also matches `NSDecimalNumber.m`:
the class factories allocate a placeholder and autorelease its initialized
result (i386 `0x42597ff0` / `0x4259802c`, PPC `0x425613a8` /
`0x42560894`). `NSDecimalNumberPlaceholder -initWithString:locale:` creates an
`NSScanner`, applies a nonnil locale, scans an `NSDecimal`, initializes from
that value on success or falls back to `init` on failure, then releases the
scanner (i386 `0x4259c790`, PPC `0x4255fb94`). No constructor correction was
indicated.

The `NSNumber` compatibility constructors also match the target paths:
signed integers convert to an unsigned magnitude plus sign and delegate to
`initWithMantissa:exponent:isNegative:`, unsigned integers delegate without a
sign, and float initialization forwards to double initialization. Double
initialization obtains an `NSNumber` decimal value before constructing the
placeholder. The `numberWithLongLong:` and `numberWithDouble:` factories allocate
the placeholder, initialize it, and autorelease the result. Representative
addresses: i386 `initWithLongLong:` `0x4259ca28`, `initWithDouble:`
`0x4259c91c`, `numberWithLongLong:` `0x42598550`, `numberWithDouble:`
`0x4259841c`; PPC `initWithLongLong:` `0x425c05fc`, `initWithDouble:`
`0x4255fb0c`, `numberWithLongLong:` `0x425b9218`, `numberWithDouble:`
`0x425b9070`. No constructor correction was indicated.

Paired IDA review of the concrete representation methods also matches source:
`initWithDecimal:` compacts the value, allocates an `NSDecimalNumber` with
space for its mantissa words in the placeholder's zone, and copies the decimal
after the object pointer (i386 `0x4255307c`, PPC `0x4255b000`). The mantissa
initializer builds the exponent, sign, length, and words before delegating
(i386 `0x4259c6d0`, PPC `0x425c039c`). `decimalValue` copies the stored struct,
and localized description forwards the struct at `self + 4` to
`NSDecimalString` (i386 `0x4259bec4` / `0x4259befc`, PPC `0x4255ad28` /
`0x4255bbc4`). No representation correction was indicated.

Paired IDA review of `NSDecimalNumber` coding matches the source's wire fields:
exponent, four-bit length, sign, compact flag, a word count of eight, and all
eight mantissa words. `NSDecimalNumberPlaceholder -initWithCoder:` decodes
those fields, reconstructs the `NSDecimal` flags, decodes the mantissa array,
and delegates to `initWithDecimal:`. The base `NSDecimalNumber -initWithCoder:`
raises the concrete-initializer error, while `classForCoder` and
`replacementObjectForCoder:` preserve the public class and identity. Addresses:
i386 encode `0x4259bfc4`, placeholder decode `0x425530f0`, base decode
`0x4259c114`; PPC encode `0x425bfa1c`, placeholder decode `0x425c0260`, base
decode `0x425bfbac`. No coding correction was indicated.

Paired IDA review of `NSDecimalNumber` arithmetic confirms addition,
subtraction, multiplication, division, power, and power-of-ten methods fetch the
behavior scale and rounding mode, call the matching `NSDecimal` operation, and
share the same error-handler/rounding/result-construction flow as
`NSDecimalNumberFinishOperation`. `decimalNumberByRoundingAccordingToBehavior:`
retains and autoreleases the receiver for `NSDecimalNoScale`; otherwise it
rounds and constructs a new number. `compare:` uses the stored decimal directly
for decimal-number operands and converts other numbers through `decimalValue`.
Representative i386 addresses: add `0x4259b818`, subtract `0x4259be3c`,
multiply `0x4259b9f8`, divide `0x4259b908`, power `0x4259bbe4`, compare
`0x4259b72c`. PPC: add `0x425bf180`, subtract `0x425bf83c`, multiply
`0x425bf3f8`, divide `0x425bf2bc`, power `0x425bf670`, compare `0x4255a4fc`.
No arithmetic-wrapper correction was indicated.

Paired IDA review of the numeric accessors matches `NSDecimalNumber.m`'s
target-specific conversions. Both targets accumulate the mantissa and apply
the decimal exponent in `doubleValue`; i386 uses extended precision internally,
while PPC uses `double`. Signed accessors truncate through the corresponding

`0x425bf924`, `unsignedIntValue` `0x425bffb8`, `getValue:` `0x425bfb70`. No

Paired IDA review confirms the `NSScanner scanDecimal:` wrapper and decimal

scan location and commits both the decimal result and new location only after

`0x425a2950`, PPC `0x4255dbf8`. No scanDecimal correction was indicated.

The thread-local behavior accessors also match both IDA targets:

## PPC decimal table paths beyond the contiguous raw span

PPC's contiguous raw divisor snapshot ends at reduced index 19,452, but the
paired scan retains count classifications and exact divisors through index
26,363. Positive direct calls use later rows when each required nonzero
divisor is recorded (at most 48 words), or when an earlier zero count has
emptied the intermediate mantissa. Later unknown divisor words are then
unread because `NSIntegerMultiply` returns on its zero-length operand. An
unrecorded nonzero divisor before the first zero still uses the bounded
fallback.

Update (2026-10-08): extended the PPC row scan through reduced index 26,768.
Indices 26,441–26,479 remain in `__OBJC,__sel_backref` and contribute eight
zero rows, eleven complete divisors of at most 48 words (13 words total), and
twenty count-only rows with larger divisors. The following rows through 26,768
have zero count words in the file-backed zero-filled tail of the `__OBJC`
segment; index 26,768's row begins eight bytes before the segment boundary, so
its two-byte count fits with six bytes remaining, while index 26,769 begins
beyond the segment. `NSDecimal.m` now models that exact range, extending the
PPC table lookup ceiling to 26,768 and the original-power preflight ceiling to
26,806 (`26,768 + 38`). The source preflight still admits each positive or
negative call only when its required divisor reads are represented or
unreachable; this is not a guarantee that every call through the ceiling
takes the mapped path. i386 remains unchanged. Static IDA/Mach-O/source
comparison and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

formatting remains observable. Static paired IDA/source review and

## PPC `NSTimeZonePeriod` offset and daylight flag encoding (resolved)

The i386 parser (`+[NSConcreteTimeZone parseTimeZoneData:into:count:zone:]`,
`0x425366d8`) stores the daylight flag in bit 31 and the signed offset in the
remaining 31 bits; its accessors decode that layout (`secondsFromGMTForDate:`

(`0x425b85bc`) instead stores `(offset << 1) | daylight`, as confirmed by its
accessors (`secondsFromGMTForDate:` `0x425be1d8`,
`isDaylightSavingTimeForDate:` `0x425bdfac`), which arithmetic-shift right one
and read bit 0, respectively. `NSTimeZone.m` now uses the i386 layout on i386
and the packed offset-shifted layout on PPC in the parser and both accessors.

## `NSRunLoop -limitDateForMode:`

The i386 body (`0x4251080c`) and PPC body (`0x42517018`) run performers and

time, then release the vector and restore `_currentMode`, including on an
exception path. `NSRunLoop.m` follows the same ordering and cleanup. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

invalidate that mode's cached delegate vector when membership changes, and
update the process-wide Mach port set under its lock. Removing a mode's last
occurrence removes one global vector reference and removes the Mach port from
the set only when no other global reference remains. The source's helper calls
preserve these duplicate-reference and port-set rules on both targets. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMultiReadUniWriteLock` packed state is architecture-specific

The i386 and PPC implementations store active-reader and active-writer state in
`_priv[12]` using different bit layouts. i386 (`init` `0x4258016c`, reader
acquire `0x425801cc`, writer acquire `0x42580238`, reader/writer try-locks
`0x425802b0`/`0x4258030c`, unlock `0x42580354`) uses the high bit of byte
`_priv + 51` as the writer flag and the low 31 bits of word `_priv[12]` as the
reader count. PPC (`init` `0x42595348`, reader acquire `0x42595390`, writer
acquire `0x4259542c`, reader/writer try-locks `0x425954f0`/`0x42595570`,
unlock `0x425955e8`) uses bit 0 of `_priv[12]` as the writer flag and bits
31:1 as the reader count. Its description reports `_priv[12] >> 1` readers and
`_priv[12] & 1` writers (`0x425952d4`). `NSLock.m` now has architecture-guarded
packing, initialization, description, acquisition, try-lock, and unlock paths
for those layouts; see “NSMultiReadUniWriteLock PPC packed-state correction”
below. This diagnosis is retained as the historical finding, not an open
divergence.

## `NSMultiReadUniWriteLock` PPC packed-state correction

`NSLock.m` now keeps the i386 writer flag in byte `_priv + 51` and reader
count in the low 31 bits of `_priv[12]`, while the PPC branch uses bit 0 for
the writer flag and bits 31:1 for active readers. PPC initialization clears
`_priv[12]`; descriptions, blocking acquisition, try-locks, and unlock now use

## `NSIntegerDivide` normalized multiword algorithm reconstructed (2026-10-08)

The i386 implementation (`0x425a1748`) and PPC implementation
(`0x425c4df4`) share a normalized base-2^16 division path after the
zero-divisor, dividend-smaller, and one-word-divisor cases. They scale both
operands by `0x10000 / (highDivisorWord + 1)`, estimate quotient words from
the top two normalized dividend words, correct each estimate at most twice
using the next divisor word, then subtract the divisor window and add it back
if the subtraction borrows. Their local work arrays hold 18 words; operands
longer than 16 words use zone-allocated work arrays. i386 sizes those arrays
as `2 * (unsigned short)(length + 1)` bytes, while PPC uses
`(2 * (length + 1)) & 0x1fffe`. The estimate-correction guards also differ:
i386 tests the second correction against the pre-decrement estimate, PPC
against the post-decrement estimate.

Following user approval, `NSIntegerDivide` in `NSDecimal.m` now follows this
normalized word path, including target-sized stack/dynamic workspaces,
quotient-estimate corrections, subtraction/add-back, and quotient trimming.
The second correction guard preserves the equivalent i386 pre-decrement and
PPC post-decrement conditions. The caller paths in `NSDecimalDivide` and
`NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` continue to match both binaries. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC natural-language date two-digit year semantics (2026-10-08)

`+[NSCalendarDate dateWithNaturalLanguageString:date:locale:]` reads the cached
`NSUseExcelTwoDigitYearSemantics` preference on PPC before token processing.
When a numeric token is assigned to the year field by the locale's date order,
the default Excel behavior maps 00–29 to 2000–2029 and 30–99 to 1930–1999;
when disabled, two-digit years receive 1900. DR2 i386 always adds 1900. The
natural-language parser now initializes and applies that cache under the PPC
compiler guard; its i386 behavior is unchanged. Confirmed in PPC
`0x425b724c` and i386 `0x425969d0`. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## Natural-language date-order cache and invalid-order handling (2026-10-08)

The i386 (`0x425a376c`) and PPC (`0x425c6eac`)
`_buildTokenMapWithDictionary` bodies update `_NumberOrder` only when
`NSDateTimeOrdering` is present; a missing key preserves the prior order. The
initial `_NumberOrder` storage is zeroed in both images (`0x42602740` i386,
`0x42626728` PPC). The natural-language date method returns nil when an
unassigned numeric component must be mapped but the order is still zero, and
returns nil for an order character other than Y, M, D, or H. `NSCalendarDate.m`
previously cleared the cached order on a missing key, substituted `MDY`, and
silently skipped unknown order characters. It now preserves the cache, leaves
the initial order unset, rejects numeric fallback when no order exists, and
rejects invalid order characters. Both targets store the order in four
zero-initialized `unichar` slots, clear them and copy the first four uppercase
characters when the key exists, and inspect four positions during numeric
fallback. The source uses the same fixed-width buffer and no longer retains an
NSString for this cache.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

Compared PPC `_NSDecimalRound` (`0x4255c52c`) with `NSDecimalRound` and its
helpers in `NSDecimal.m`. The target copies the input, drops digits through

exponent, and compacts. The source follows these paths. Static PPC IDA/source

`_NSArrayRaiseBoundException`, using the method proem and the format
`"%@: index (%d) beyond bounds (%d)"`. The source had separate range messages
and a different object-index message. Bulk reads directly `memmove` the packed
item buffer for the two concrete array classes; other array implementations
cache the `objectAtIndex:` IMP and walk the requested range. `subarrayWithRange:`
uses the same concrete count and range path, a 128-object stack buffer, and the
array factory. The source now follows these target behaviors. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSArray range-search storage and equality paths (2026-10-09)

Compared `indexOfObject:range:identical:` (i386 `0x42506304`, PPC
`0x4250c930`), its `_ArrayIndexOfObject` helpers (i386 `0x425054b4`, PPC
`0x42506aa8`), and `_NSArrayIndexOfObject` (i386 `0x42533e64`, PPC
`0x425548bc`) with `NSArray.m`. Both targets use the packed count and shared
bounds-exception helper for concrete arrays, scan the concrete item buffer,
and use a 128-item stack buffer plus `getObjects:range:` for non-concrete
arrays, allocating a zone buffer for larger ranges. The search checks pointer
identity first and, unless identity-only mode is requested, sends `isEqual:`
to the searched object with each item. The source previously called `count`
and `objectAtIndex:` for every item and raised a different range message; it
now follows the paired count, buffer, and comparison paths. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSConcreteArray initializer exception and receiver paths (2026-10-09)

Compared `NSConcreteArray initWithObjects:count:` (i386 `0x4250dc64`, PPC
`0x42511318`) and `NSConcreteMutableArray initWithObjects:count:` (i386
`0x4251981c`, PPC `0x42529fe8`) with `NSArray.m`. Both targets reject counts above
`0x7ffffff` through `_NSArrayRaiseSizeException` with the `count` label and
reject nil elements through `_NSArrayRaiseInsertNilException`; the source had
used custom messages for both cases. The mutable initializer also uses the
receiver returned by `initWithCapacity:` before allocating and filling storage;
the source had ignored that return value. The source now follows these helper,
cleanup, ownership, and receiver paths. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

`NSDtoa.m` provides the PPC `___dtoa` conversion routine and quotient helper.
A paired comparison against PPC IDA (`0x4254e138`, `_quorem` at `0x4255b5e0`)
confirmed matching special-value handling, exponent estimation, fast and

`NSLanguageContext.m` matches both IDA targets for named-context caching,

`+[NSHTTPURLHandle canonicalHTTPURLForURL:]` now returns early when the

`NSNotificationCenter -applyCallBack:context:name:object:literally:` now

`NSNotificationCenter -removeObserver:name:object:` now matches both target

`NSNotificationCenter -addObserver:selector:name:object:flags:` now obtains
its cached callback using `_NSIMPForObjectAndSelector`, matching i386

`NSNotificationCenter -_bundleLoaded` now returns before locking when its

`NSNotificationCenter _redoTables` now preserves the architecture split seen
in IDA: PPC (`0x425377b8`) frees and clears the old nil-name table on a

`NSConnection -insertProxy:` now checks a local proxy's `name` class without a

`NSConnection -insertProxy:` now logs newly inserted proxies when connection

log follows the table unlock and reports wire kind, class name, proxy, target,
and connection.

`NSConnection -insertProxy:` raises `NSInternalInconsistencyException` for its

(`0x4252c8f8`) use the same messages for an invalid wire value, a mismatched
connection, and a local proxy whose target is an `NSDistantObject`; source now
matches those exception names and format strings.

## `NSConnection` proxy conversion parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `proxyForObject:` and `proxyWithLocal:` in i386 IDA (`0x42567f40`,

## `NSUserDefaults` search, registration, and snapshot parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `searchList`, `setSearchList:`, `registerDefaults:`,
`dictionaryRepresentation`, and `synchronize` in i386 IDA (`0x42566198`,
`0x4254c9c4`, `0x42543580`, `0x42537af8`, `0x4253b5e8`) and PPC IDA
(`0x4257127c`, `0x42540e10`, `0x4253e088`, `0x425556ec`, `0x42544654`)
with `NSUserDefaults.m`. The methods preserve copy/autorelease ownership for
search-list snapshots, recompute `_dictRep` after search-list changes, merge
registration defaults only when the registration domain is searched, and
rebuild the dictionary snapshot under the lock. PPC creates the registration
dictionary with capacity and adds the old and new entries; i386 mutable-copies
the old dictionary. Registration-change notification is posted after unlock
on PPC and before unlock on i386, as the source guards specify. Source matches
both target flows. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSUserDefaults` persistent-domain operation parity (2026-10-15)

(`0x42565f78`) and PPC IDA (`0x42571048`) with
`NSUserDefaults.m`. Setting rejects reserved names and existing volatile
domains under the lock, unlocks before raising, writes the domain, and rebuilds

Removal checks persistent-domain existence before locking, then removes,
conditionally rebuilds the dictionary, unlocks, and conditionally posts. The
source matches both targets. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or

## `NSUserDefaults` volatile-domain operation parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `setVolatileDomain:forName:` in i386 IDA (`0x42540124`) and PPC IDA

## `NSUserDefaults` domain-query ownership parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `volatileDomainNames`, `volatileDomainForName:`,

`NSConnection -portalDied:` now logs the connection, notification object, and

`NSDistantObject -retain` increments the PPC 24-bit refcount field without

`NSDistantObject -_anticipateRelease` logs
`piggybacking [0x%x _releaseWireCount:%u]` before releasing a nonzero

`NSDistantObject -encodeWithCoder:` creates a counterpart local proxy through

`NSDistantObject -dealloc` logs `deallocing %x` after releasing its connection
when distant-object logging is enabled, matching i386 (`0x42549f3c`) and PPC
(`0x4253cb84`).

`+[NSDistantObject newDistantObjectWithCoder:]` now fetches the coder's

`NSStringArray -initWithArray:` allocates its encoding buffer when capacity

`+[NSStringArray stringArray]` returns the startup-owned `__NSEmptyStringArray`

once before packed-data validation, and allocates decoded strings with

cutoff and sends `bytes` and `length` before checking for nil data, matching

`NSStringArray -initWithWordsOfData:convertCase:locale:` preserves the target

`NSStringArray -UTF8Data` returns `[NSData data]` when the backing data is nil,
matching i386 (`0x42561394`) and PPC (`0x4256b7e0`).

`NSStringArray -stringArrayByAppendingStringArray:` checks the argument's
backing-data pointer before sending `appendData:`, including for a non-nil

`NSStringArray -stringArrayByAppendingStringArrays:resultingBitVectors:` now
receives a +1 bit vector from its helper, adds it to the output array when

`0x425647ec` and PPC `0x4256f084`.

`NSStringArray -dealloc` obtains its iteration count through `[self count]`

`NSStringArray -count` logs the target invariant diagnostic when valid packed

`NSStringArray -initWithArray:` checks the cached `__NSStringArrayClass`

`_NSUTF8ASCIIString -characterAtIndex:` and `-getCharacters:range:` use the

`NSStringArray -count` and `-objectAtIndex:` reject malformed packed UTF-8

## PPC geometry parser missing-component correction (2026-10-09)

A recheck of `NSPointFromString`, `NSSizeFromString`, and `NSRectFromString`
found that the earlier parser note omitted the missing-component behavior.
PPC calls `__NSstrtod` for each requested field even after scanning reaches the
terminator; no-token conversion returns zero. Updated `NSGeometryParsePPC` to
store that result and advance the cursor for every field, so incomplete input
no longer leaves geometry components uninitialized. This preserves the
reference's permissive numeric parsing and does not change the i386 scanner
path. Static IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSInsetRect` sequential inset arithmetic (2026-10-09)

The i386 (`0x42510014`) and PPC (`0x42514e18`) reference bodies subtract each
inset twice in sequence. PPC instructions use two single-precision `fsubs`
operations per dimension. `NSGeometry.m` had multiplied each inset by the
double literal `2.0`, which can produce a different rounding result. The
source now preserves the target operation order for width and height. Static
paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` scalar encoding parity (2026-10-09)

The i386 helper (`0x42522e80`) and PPC helper (`0x4250bffc`) return size and
alignment 4 for `!` and `%`, and size/alignment 1 for `$`. They return
size/alignment 0 for `B`, `v`, `?`, and unknown encodings. `NSObjCRuntime.m`
previously treated `!`, `%`, and `$` as unknown, and gave `B`, `v`, and `?`
non-target results. Added the confirmed scalar cases and aligned unknown
results to match both targets. PPC union size selection and aggregate bitfield
packing are recorded in the paired helper comparison below. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## PPC `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` leading-double struct alignment (2026-10-09)

PPC `__NSGetSizeAndAlignment` (`0x4250bffc`) initializes a struct double
alignment to 4, changes it to 8 only when the first field is `d`, and uses
that alignment for subsequent doubles. i386 (`0x42522e80`) uses the scalar
double alignment of 4 for every field. `NSSizeAndAlignmentOfType` now applies
the leading-double rule under the PPC build guard, matching the target field
padding and final struct alignment while preserving i386 behavior. The PPC
qualifier scan also includes `r`, so a leading `const double` selects the same
alignment. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests
or builds were run.

## `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` union and bitfield layout parity (2026-10-09)

The i386 helper `_getBitfieldSizeAndAdvance` (`0x425767b4`) and PPC helper
(`0x425888c0`) both pack consecutive `bN` fields into 32-bit units, return
alignment 4, pad zero-width fields to a word boundary, and restart a field
when it crosses the remaining bits in a word. The aggregate walkers pass the
current byte offset and add the helper's rounded byte count. The source now
uses the same run-based helper rather than treating each `bN` independently.

Both target helpers return a union's maximum ordinary member size without a
final size round-up and exclude bitfields from that maximum. The original PPC
review incorrectly concluded that `double` fields were also excluded from the
union maximum. The 2026-10-12 instruction-level recheck below corrects that
conclusion: PPC includes each parsed non-bitfield size, including `double`,
while its alignment still follows the leading-double rule. Direct `b` encodings
follow each target's unknown-type result. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` malformed aggregate and array paths (2026-10-09)

i386 `__NSGetSizeAndAlignment` (`0x42522e80`) and PPC (`0x4250bffc`) raise
`NSInvalidArgumentException` with `badly formed array description` when an
array element encoding is not followed by `]` (reference strings at
`0x425fcbb6` and `0x4261fa0c`). Both helpers also raise the forward-use
reason when a struct or union closes before `=`, but only when size or
alignment output is requested; reaching the terminator before `=` raises the
parsing-error reason unconditionally. If a defined aggregate reaches its
terminator without a closing delimiter, both increment past that terminator
and return. `NSSizeAndAlignmentOfType` now follows those validation and cursor
paths. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or
builds were run.

## `NSGetSizeAndAlignment` array element stride (2026-10-09)

Both i386 (`0x42522e80`) and PPC (`0x4250bffc`) round each array element size
up to its reported alignment before multiplying by the element count. The
source previously multiplied the count by the raw element size, which differed
for unions whose maximum member size is not aligned to the union alignment.
`NSSizeAndAlignmentOfType` now uses the target stride formula. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## i386 `NSMethodSignature` argument-record write order (2026-10-09)

i386 `+[NSMethodSignature signatureWithObjCTypes:]` (`0x42520c88`) stores each
argument type, calls `__NSGetSizeAndAlignment` directly into the argument size
slot, then stores the current frame offset and advances the frame length by the
four-byte-rounded size. `_NSMethodSignatureComplete` previously wrote the offset
before parsing and copied a local size afterward. Reordered the source writes to
match the target, including the partial record state if type parsing raises.
PPC uses its separate completion path. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMethodSignature` cache hash byte signedness (2026-10-09)

The i386 `NSMethodSignature` key-callback table at `0x42603298` points to
`_hashStr` (`0x4251c390`) and `_equalStr` (`0x42521560`); PPC callback data at
`0x426272bc` points to `_hashStr` (`0x42516e70`) and `_equalStr`
(`0x42522110`). Both hash helpers convert each input byte through signed `char`
to `unsigned short` before the rolling hash. `NSMethodSignature.m` previously
hashed each byte as `unsigned char`, producing different cache hashes for bytes
at or above 0x80. The source now sign-extends each byte to 16 bits, matching
both targets. The wildcard structural equality callbacks also match the source
comparison loop. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only;
no tests or builds were run.

## `NSPathStore2` append error diagnostics (2026-10-09)

i386 and PPC `NSPathStore2` use the same error strings and argument order for
`stringByAppendingPathComponent:` and `stringByAppendingPathExtension:`. The
component error is `%@: cannot append path '%@' to path '%@'`; the extension
error is `%@: cannot append extension '%@' to path '%@'`. Both log the method
proem, attempted value, and original path. Source previously used shorter
strings and omitted the path argument. Updated to match the target calls.
Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `_NSFileAccessModes` output-word architecture split (2026-10-09)

The optional two-word output from `_NSFileAccessModes` differs by target after
successful path conversion and `stat`: i386 stores `st_ctimespec.tv_nsec` and
`st_birthtimespec.tv_sec`, while PPC writes the 64-bit `st_size` value. The
source now preserves the i386 output and uses a PPC-guarded copy of
`status.st_size`. The return value also differs when an access output is
requested: i386 returns the raw final `access()` result; PPC returns the final
Boolean success value. Source now preserves these target-specific results.
Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile _setDictionary:forDomain:` write retry parity (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x4253c1c4`) and PPC (`0x4254527c`). Both initialize the
serialization buffer with capacity `0x2000`, retry atomic writes up to three
times, and log failed writes with `"%@: Could not write to %@: %d"` (i386
string `0x425f87cc`, PPC `0x4261b0cc`). The final retry message is
`"%@: Could not write data, giving up on %@"` (i386 string `0x425f87ea`, PPC
`0x4261b0ec`). Source previously used capacity 1024 and omitted the errno and
colon in both diagnostics. The source now matches the buffer size, log formats,
and arguments. On write failure, i386 reads `cthread_errno()` before calling
`_NSMethodExceptionProem`; PPC calls the proem first. The guarded source order
preserves this architecture split. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile allDomains` lazy result construction (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x42538308`) and PPC (`0x4256ff6c`). Both obtain cached domain
keys before requesting the directory listing. They keep the mutable result nil
when the listing is nil and allocate it only when a cached nonempty domain must
be added, initializing it with that first domain. If neither source yields a
domain, both return `[NSArray array]`; otherwise they copy the mutable result
into an immutable array and release it. The source previously requested the
directory listing first and eagerly allocated an empty mutable array with
capacity 8. Reordered the calls and matched the lazy allocation and empty
result paths. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile removeObjectForKey:domain:` missing dirty-list path (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x4254176c`) and PPC (`0x4257037c`). After removing a cached
key, both targets update the dirty-key array only when that array already
exists. If the marker lookup returns nil, neither target creates a replacement
marker. Source previously marked the whole domain dirty in that case. Removed
that fallback so the method follows both target paths. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile domainExists:` manager call-order split (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x4253f698`) and PPC (`0x425373f4`). Both read the cache entry
once and return whether its dictionary is nonempty when present. If absent,
i386 constructs the `.plist` path before calling the default file-manager
factory; PPC obtains the manager first, then constructs the path. Source
previously read the same cache entry twice and always built the path first. It
now caches the first lookup and preserves the target manager/path order under
the PPC guard. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile _dictionaryForDomain:` empty-file release path (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x42525888`) and PPC (`0x425337d4`). When the loaded property
list data has zero length, both targets remove the domain and return nil before
the common release at the end of the deserialization path. The source also
released the data on this branch. Removed that release to match the binaries;
this preserves their empty-file leak. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile _dictionaryForDomain:` failure diagnostic path (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x42525888`) and PPC (`0x425337d4`). Both build the domain's
`.plist` path once, load from that path, and pass the same path as the second
argument to the deserialization-failure log together with the method proem.
Source passed the bare domain name to the log. It now retains the resolved path
for both file loading and diagnostics. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSUserDefaults` persistent/volatile domain conflict diagnostics (2026-10-09)

Compared `setPersistentDomain:forName:` in i386 (`0x425665dc`) and PPC
(`0x42561128`), and `setVolatileDomain:forName:` in i386 (`0x42540124`) and
PPC (`0x42571b7c`). Both targets use three format arguments: the method proem,

(i386 string `0x425f8938`, PPC `0x4261b254`). Source used different wording and

targets. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests
or builds were run.

## `NSLockedPropertyListFile _removeDomain:` deletion path (2026-10-09)

Compared i386 (`0x425652e4`) and PPC (`0x4256febc`). Both append `.plist` to

## `NSSerialization.m` `_NSDeserializeObject` collections (i386 and PPC)

threshold zero. When nested array values or dictionary pairs deserialize to

values, while i386 uses immutable/eager defaults. `NSSerialization.m` now
follows those paths. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds

## `NSZoneCalloc` allocation and statistics call

`NSZoneCalloc` in i386 (`0x425156d8`) and PPC (`0x42511444`) defaults a null
zone, allocates `numElems * byteSize` through the zone's allocation slot, and
zeros the returned memory. When statistics are enabled, both pass event 17,
the allocation pointer, zone, total size, and a trailing zero to
`NSRecordAllocationEvent`. PPC Hex-Rays omits the variadic arguments, but its
disassembly loads all four values into `r4`–`r7`; i386 pushes the same values.
`NSZone.m` matches both targets. No source correction was indicated. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` mapped-table limits (superseded, 2026-10-10)

At the time of this note, the earlier positive and negative power entries that
gave a common 26,401 boundary had been superseded by the PPC tail scan. The
source then modeled reduced divisor rows through 26,363 on i386 and 26,768 on
PPC, so the guarded
original-power preflight caps are 26,401 and 26,806 respectively. Those caps
do not imply every call within the range uses the mapped path: positive calls
must have each reached divisor span represented or become unreachable after a
zero intermediate, and negative calls must pass the divisor-versus-dividend
preflight. Calls rejected by those gates continue through the bounded fallback.
These boundaries follow `NSDecimalReferencePowerTableDivisor`,
`NSDecimalPositivePowerTableSpansAvailable`, and
`NSDecimalMappedNegativePowerAvailable` in `NSDecimal.m`, and the PPC
file-backed segment scan recorded above. Static source/IDA review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` i386 count-only divisor tail (superseded)

IDA reads the i386 power-table count word at `_pow10` (`0x425bba04`) plus
18 bytes per reduced index. Rows 26,364 through 26,422 contain the mapped
word `0xffff`; row 26,363 is zero. `NSIntegerDivide` calls
`NSIntegerCompare`, which compares operand lengths before reading divisor
words and clears the quotient when the dividend is shorter. At this stage,
`NSDecimal.m` modeled those 59 rows as count-only divisors and admitted negative
powers through -26,460 when the current length was below 65,535; the first
required row was 26,422. PPC was then capped at -26,806 because its next count
word was outside the captured segment. The complete signed-short raw-image
reconstruction below supersedes these limits. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` format scanner and positional-mode bounds (2026-10-10)

Compared the scanner in `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` in i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) with `NSMutableString.m`. Both targets read UTF-16 input in chunks of at most 32 code units, retain at most nine positional conversion records, and cap each conversion token at 31 bytes including `%`; sequential conversions reuse one record and are substituted inline. Internal positional argument handling recognizes one-digit indexes 1–9. A positional value index selects positional mode only on the first conversion record; positional star indexes alone do not select it, and a later positional index does not switch a format already parsed in sequential mode. The source scanner and record handling match these limits and transitions. Together with the conversion-class audit above, source-to-target dispatch and argument-width handling are accounted for; exhaustive libc formatting results remain outside this static comparison. No source correction indicated. No tests or builds were run.
## `NSMutableString` mixed sequential and positional format mode (2026-10-10)

The i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) scanners enter positional mode only when a positional value index appears in the first conversion record. Once a sequential conversion has set the parser state to sequential, a later `%N$` token is normalized but does not switch argument selection to positional mode. `NSMutableString.m` previously set its global `positional` flag unconditionally during the second token pass, so a later positional conversion incorrectly reinterpreted earlier and later arguments. The source now switches modes there only for the first conversion record; its earlier detection already handles `%N$` while the first token is being scanned. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` sequential substitution order (2026-10-10)

Compared `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` in i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`). Both targets call `SubstituteFormat` immediately after parsing each sequential conversion, then advance the argument pointer for width, precision, and value arguments. They reuse one conversion record for this path; positional mode stores records for deferred substitution. `NSMutableString.m` now substitutes each sequential token during scanning, adjusts subsequent source offsets for earlier replacements, and advances its local argument pointer afterward. The positional pass is covered by the paired audit below. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` positional argument substitution pass (2026-10-10)

Rechecked the positional pass in `setStringWithFormat:locale:arguments:` for i386 (`0x4250ab70`) and PPC (`0x4250f9dc`) against `NSMutableString.m`. Both targets collect at most nine conversion records, build an argument-pointer table using the conversion classes and 4-byte/8-byte advances, resolve positional width and precision arguments before value substitution, then apply records in source order while adjusting offsets for prior replacements. The source follows that flow: `NSStringFormatResolveStars` advances the indexed argument pointer, `NSStringFormatRemoveArgumentIndex` removes the value selector, and the deferred loop updates offsets after each replacement. `_IncrementArgPointer` (`0x4250cc14` i386, `0x4250a9bc` PPC), `_SubstituteIntArgument` (`0x42593324` i386, `0x425ab044` PPC), and `_SubstituteFormat` (`0x42511bd8` i386, `0x42509ab0` PPC) confirm the source helpers' argument widths, star clamping, and conversion dispatch. This closes the earlier staged positional-pass review; libc formatting results remain outside the static comparison. No source correction indicated. No tests or builds were run.

## `NSMutableString` sequential star argument advancement (2026-10-10)

The same i386 and PPC bodies track width and precision stars with separate Boolean fields, then advance the sequential argument pointer once per field. The source previously counted every `*` character, so repeated stars in one field advanced too many slots. It now tracks whether a width star and/or precision star occurred and uses those flags for cursor advancement. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSString -lossyCString` buffer growth (2026-10-10)

DR2 i386 (`0x4253076c`) and MOSXS PPC (`0x425a80cc`) both start conversion in
a 500-byte stack buffer. If characters remain, each grows capacity by
`capacity + ((remainingLength + 1) * capacity / max(consumedLength, 1)) + 100`,
then stores output in `NSMutableData`, extending it as needed. Both terminate
the final buffer with NUL; the no-growth path copies the stack bytes into an
autoreleased allocation. An empty input returns the static empty string's
bytes. `NSStringEncodings.m` now follows these paths instead of doubling a
private allocation on every growth. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` file-backed signed-short reads (2026-10-10 addendum, superseded)

This investigation led to the raw-image snapshot design implemented in the
complete signed-short divisor image entry below.

Correction to the earlier captured-table wording: the original i386 and PPC Mach-O files contain readable, file-backed bytes beyond the IDA initialized-data boundary. For positive powers through `SHRT_MAX`, the highest table row selected is 32,729; the full count-sized read spans end at `0x42668432` on i386 and `0x42691254` on PPC, both within readable `__LINKEDIT`. Negating `SHRT_MIN` in the target's signed 16-bit temporary wraps, so `-32768` instead reads before `_pow10`: i386 row `0x4252ba04` has count 13, PPC row `0x425525d8` has count 48,001, and both payloads remain within readable `__TEXT`. Thus exact target bytes are available for signed-short reads, but they are adjacent image data rather than semantic power-table entries. In-image callers remain bounded to small powers; the edge concerns direct calls to the private helper. The exact raw-image snapshot design was subsequently implemented in `NSDecimal.m`; see `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` complete signed-short divisor image below. No tests or builds were run.

## `_NSIntegerMultiplyByPowerOf10` raw-image signed-short reconstruction (2026-10-10)

The approved raw-image design is implemented in `NSDecimal.m`. IDA confirms both architectures read divisor counts at `_pow10 + 18 * power`; the i386 `-8` expression belongs to positive capacity preflight. Added exact target-endian raw slices for the high table rows and the signed-short wraparound read. i386 tail rows 26,423–32,729 span `0x4262fbe2` through (exclusive) `0x42668432`; the maximum count-sized span is row 32,542 with count 60,680. PPC rows 26,769–32,729 span `0x4265800a` through (exclusive) `0x42691254`; the maximum is row 32,605 with count 64,504. The `SHRT_MIN` read spans are `0x4252ba04`–`0x4252ba20` (i386, count 13) and `0x425525d8`–`0x42569cdc` (PPC, count 48,001). These full-span checks confirm the endpoints and maximum rows recorded in the signed-short image-bounds note.

The lookup now returns exact high-tail rows, the mapped-path preflights admit the complete non-minimum signed-short range, and `SHRT_MIN` performs the target's final divide with its exact adjacent-image count and payload. In-image callers remain within their previously confirmed small power bounds. Byte-for-byte comparison against both original Mach-O slices, full count-span bounds checks, and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

At this intermediate stage, the signed-short source path still used a bounded
mathematical fallback when an earlier row was count-only or its complete
divisor span was unavailable. The complete signed-short divisor image below
supersedes that fallback; it covers the full non-minimum reduction range, and
the separate `SHRT_MIN` slice captures its wrapped read.

This supersedes the earlier high-tail-only snapshot and incomplete-span fallback notes. These slices contain rows 39–32,729; IDA confirms divisor counts are read at `_pow10 + 18 * power`. The existing `SHRT_MIN` slices are retained at i386 `[0x4252ba04, 0x4252ba20)` and PPC `[0x425525d8, 0x42569cdc)`.

The helper and preflight checks now cover every row reached by representable non-minimum signed-short inputs without using the bounded mathematical fallback. ## `NSDecimal` core word arithmetic paired review (2026-10-10)

Rechecked `_NSIntegerMultiply` (i386 `0x425a1c14`, PPC `0x425c5280`),
`_NSIntegerAdd` (i386 `0x425a1510`, PPC `0x425c4c6c`),
`_NSIntegerSubtract` (i386 `0x425a2020`, PPC `0x425c5690`), and
`_NSIntegerDivide` (i386 `0x425a1748`, PPC `0x425c4df4`) against
`NSDecimal.m`. Multiply uses a temporary when the destination aliases the
left operand, accumulates base-2^16 products, trims high zero words, then
copies back; add propagates carry and checks destination capacity only for a
final carry; subtraction propagates borrow, returns overflow when the final
borrow is clear, and trims only on success. Division keeps the zero,
smaller-dividend, and one-word-divisor cases, then normalizes both operands,
estimates and corrects quotient digits, subtracts the divisor window, adds it
back on borrow, and trims the quotient. Source matches both target paths,
including i386/PPC workspace-size expressions and their equivalent
quotient-estimate correction guards. Static paired IDA/source review only; no
tests or builds were run.

## `NSInvocation` object-layout ABI follow-up (2026-10-11)

The earlier `NSInvocation` entry left object ABI compatibility unverified.
Static comparison of `NSInvocation.h`, `NSInvocationInstance` in
`NSInvocation.m`, and the i386/PPC ABI records confirms a 36-byte object with
`returnValue` at offset 4, `argumentFrame` at 16, `signature` at 20,
`container` at 24, packed flags/refcount at 28–31, and `reserved` at 32. The
12-byte `NSObjCValue` field follows from its 4-byte tag plus 8-byte maximum
union and matches the target offset of `argumentFrame`. The same comparison of
`NSMethodSignature.h`, its implementation mirror, and both ABI records confirms
a 32-byte object with fields at offsets 4 through 28 in 4-byte increments.
This closes the static object-layout concern; it does not establish runtime
behavior. Static source/manifest review only; no tests or builds were run.

calling super. Source matches both targets through the cthreads timeout API
adaptation. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

(i386 `0x4256b800`, PPC `0x4257849c`) and `UniqueString` (i386
`0x4254c5bc`, PPC `0x425403a4`) with
`NSDistributedNotificationCenter.m`. Both targets decode user info, canonicalize
the object without copying, derive notification flags, and post through the
superclass; their exception path logs and releases the decoded user info, while
the unarchiver is released after a successful post. `UniqueString` lazily creates
the set, returns an existing member, and copies/inserts/releases only when
requested. `GarbageCollectUniquedStrings` is an empty function in both binaries
(i386 `0x4256eca0`, PPC `0x4257b6e8`), matching the source. No correction was
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConcreteDistantObjectRequest` ownership lifecycle parity (2026-10-13)

Compared `initWithInvocation:conversation:sequence:importedObjects:connection:`
(i386 `0x42567210`, PPC `0x425731dc`), `replyWithException:` (i386
`0x42567294`, PPC `0x42573280`), and `dealloc` (i386 `0x4256718c`, PPC
`0x4257314c`) with `NSConnection.m`. Both targets retain invocation, imported
objects, conversation, and connection in that order; reply releases and clears
the conversation before forwarding the result; deallocation releases those
four fields in order and then calls `super`. Source matches both targets. No
correction was indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or
builds were run.

## `NSConnection returnResult:exception:sequence:imports:` parity (2026-10-13)

Compared i386 (`0x425534e4`) and PPC (`0x425391cc`) IDA pseudocode with
`NSConnection.m`. Both targets return early for oneway invocations; otherwise
they encode the message identifier and sequence, encode the exception, encode
the return value only when there is no exception, invalidate the invocation,
anticipate imported-object releases, finish and send the coder before the reply
deadline, then invalidate/release it and increment the sent-reply statistic.
The exception path invalidates/releases the coder and rethrows the caught
exception. Source matches both targets. No correction was indicated. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConnection dispatchInvocation:` logging getter order (2026-10-13)

Compared i386 (`0x4254fb74`) and PPC (`0x4253a9b4`) IDA pseudocode and
disassembly with `NSConnection.m`. Both binaries re-read the invocation's
selector and target inside the entry and exception logging branches. i386 reads
selector then target; PPC reads target then selector. Source previously reused
the selector captured before logging. It now makes the target-specific getter
calls in both logging branches and preserves each architecture's order. Static
paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSConnection doQueuedWork` empty conversation-request path (2026-10-13)

Compared i386 (`0x42518c60`) and PPC (`0x4251dd18`) IDA pseudocode with
`NSConnection.m`. When the current thread has a conversation, both targets
fetch its queued conversation request and only retain it, acquire the work-queue
lock, clear the slot, unlock, and handle the request if it is nonnil. Source
previously locked and cleared the slot even when no request existed; it now
performs that state change only for a nonnil request. Static paired IDA/source
review only; no tests or builds were run.

The ordinary queue path also checks `[queue count]` before taking the lock,
then fetches and retains index 0 under the lock and removes it only when the
result is nonnil; neither target rechecks the count inside the lock. Source's
extra count check inside the lock has been removed, preserving the conditional
removal.

Compared `_NSHandleDORequest` in i386 (`0x4256a560`) and PPC (`0x425774ac`)
with `NSConnectionHandleQueuedRequest`. Both add the request conversation,
catch/log delegate exceptions before falling through to dispatch, and remove
the conversation before releasing a delegate-handled request. The unhandled
path dispatches, removes the conversation, replies, then releases the request.
Source matches both targets; no correction was indicated. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

the `_signatureValid` message for a nil invocation; it now preserves the target

The same paired review found the delegate-handled path releases the request and
