## `NSFileManager _NSOpenFileDescriptor` PPC mode-register flow (2026-10-13)

i386 `_NSOpenFileDescriptor` (`0x4254605c`) explicitly calls `open(path,
flags, mode)`. PPC Hex-Rays decompilation of `_NSOpenFileDescriptor`
(`0x42555628`) renders a two-argument call, but raw disassembly leaves `r3`,
`r4`, and `r5` unchanged before `bl _open`. Its
`initWithPath:flags:createMode:` caller (`0x4258d304`) sets `r5` to the
requested mode before calling the helper, so the runtime PPC call carries that
third word through. `NSFileManager.m` keeps the PPC two-argument call form while
retaining the i386 three-argument call. Both targets perform the same descriptor
and non-directory checks. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source
review only. Added the missing i386 source-map record; the PPC record already existed. No tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle` Java principal-class selection (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`__NSBundleAddMoreClassesAndNotify`, `0x4258492c`) and PPC

setting `_principalClass` only while it is nil. This leaves the first class in
the `NSJavaClassesForBundle` result as the principal class. `NSBundle.m` now
selects index 0 when its principal-class slot is empty. Static paired IDA/source
review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle` Java class-list allocation failure (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`__NSBundleAddJavaClasses`, `0x4258481c`) and PPC
(`0x4259aed4`) allocate a class-pointer buffer after retrieving the Java class
array. The load-complete flag and PPC class-to-bundle map are updated only if
that allocation succeeds; otherwise `_NSBundleLoadJavaCode` reports failure.
`NSBundle.m` now preserves that allocation gate before marking the load complete
or populating the map. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check`
only; no tests or builds were run.

In `-[_NSUndoInvocation description]`, i386 (`0x4256e548`) evaluates the

## `_NSUndoStack _removeBottom` pruning flow (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`0x4256e720`) and PPC (`0x4257b0f0`) start at the tail begin mark,
walk toward newer nodes while balancing begin/end marks, release each popped
node, reconnect the remaining tail, and decrement `_count`. The source's
extra empty-list and count guards did not match that flow. Its callers prune
only while `_max` is nonzero and `_count > _max`, so a remaining head is
present after removing the oldest group. `NSUndoManager.m` now follows the
paired loop and updates. Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSUndoManager setRunLoopModes:` replacement ownership order (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`0x4256cf90`) and PPC (`0x42579ec8`) save the old modes array,
copy the replacement using the receiver's zone, store the copied array, then
release the old value. `NSUndoManager.m` previously released the old array
before storing the copy; it now preserves the target ownership sequence.
Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds
were run.

## `NSConcreteMutableData` oversized argument exceptions (2026-10-13)

Both targets use the shared format `"%@: absurd %s: %d"` for oversized values.

`0x4253af1c`, `0x42595a98`, and `0x4251bd04`, respectively. Each passes the
field name (`"capacity"`, `"length"`, or `"extra length"`) and oversized value.

## `NSConcreteMutableData` VM-backed growth deallocation size (2026-10-13)

In `_NSMutableDataGrowBytes`, both i386 (`0x42526ff8`) and PPC (`0x42533df4`)
pass the current `_length` to `NSDeallocateMemoryPages` when replacing VM-backed
storage. `NSData.m` previously passed the old `_capacity`; it now passes the
captured copy length used to preserve the existing bytes. Static paired IDA
pseudocode/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSConcreteMutableData` growth capacity formula (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`_NSMutableDataGrowBytes`, `0x42526ff8`) and PPC (`0x42533df4`)
compute the growth increment from the current `_length` (half below the page
size, one quarter otherwise), then retain the old `_capacity` if that is
larger. `NSData.m` previously based the increment on old capacity and only
ensured that the result covered the length; it now follows the target formula.
The setup helper and deallocator were also compared: both targets allocate
according to `_capacity` and free VM-backed storage using `_capacity`, matching
source. Static paired IDA pseudocode/source review and `git diff --check` only;
no tests or builds were run.

## Foundation Objective-C selector parity (2026-10-13)

Ran `tools/binrecon/selector_check.py` against the MOSXS PPC Foundation binary
and DR2 i386 Foundation binary. PPC has 3,397 reference selectors and 3,397
source definitions, with no missing selectors, extras, renames, or duplicates.
i386 has 3,253 reference selectors and 3,283 source definitions, with no
missing selectors, renames, or duplicates; its 30 extras are the documented
PPC-only `NSURL` and `NSURLHandle` methods. This is selector coverage evidence,
not a comparison of method behavior. Static audit only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSBundle` resource-search language filtering (2026-10-13)

For `pathForResource:ofType:inDirectory:` (i386 `0x42578868`, PPC
`0x4258bf9c`) and `pathsForResourcesOfType:inDirectory:` (i386 `0x42578bd8`,
PPC `0x4258c34c`), both targets exclude bundle languages by sending
`arrayByExcludingToObjectsInArray:` to the system-language result. i386 reads
bundle languages before system languages; PPC reads them in the opposite

result lifetime. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only;
no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle +pathsForResourcesOfType:inDirectory:` eligibility and ownership

Both targets first call `_NSCouldBeBundle` and return the shared empty array if
the path is not a readable directory (i386 `0x42576d50`, PPC `0x425891f8`).
For eligible paths they push a local autorelease pool, prefer a `Resources`
subdirectory when present, perform the search, retain the result across pool
teardown, and autorelease it on return. `NSBundle.m` now follows this sequence
instead of making separate pre-pool existence/readability checks and returning
the search result directly. Static paired IDA/source review and
`git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle findBundleResources` setup call order (2026-10-13)

Both targets allocate the results array, read `NSInterfaceStyle`, compare it
with `windows`, and then request the default file manager (i386 `0x42527820`,
PPC `0x4251ef14`). `NSBundle.m` previously requested the file manager before
reading the style; it now follows the confirmed setup order. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle` localized resource candidate construction order (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`__NSSearchBundleDirectory` at `0x4251d838`) and PPC (`0x4250f3f4`)
construct the localized `name-` candidate only after confirming that the base
resource path exists. `NSBundleResourcePath` now defers that string operation
to the corresponding branch. The style and optional `-winnt` candidates
remain in target order. Static paired IDA/source review and

## `NSBundle findBundleResources` nil-directory handling (2026-10-13)

Neither i386 (`0x42527820`) nor PPC (`0x4251ef14`) returns early when the
directory argument is nil; the target's zero-length path buffer permits
relative resource names and language `.lproj` directories. `NSBundle.m` had a
source-only nil guard, and its NSString-based helper produced nil candidates.
The guard is removed and the helper now forms relative candidates in the nil
directory case. Static paired IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only;
no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle findBundleResources` type-count reads (2026-10-13)

IDA reads `types.count` only when a branch has a nonnull types array: once for

it across all directories. `NSBundle.m` now reads the count at each matching
root/localized branch and avoids the call when `types` is nil. Static paired
IDA/source review and `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle description` evaluation order (2026-10-13)

i386 (`0x4257878c`) reads the loaded flag, then evaluates `[self class]` and

class and bundle path first, then reads the loaded flag. `NSBundle.m` now
preserves the target-specific order. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly
and source review with `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSBundle localizedStringForKey:value:table:` cache initialization order (2026-10-13)

Both i386 (`0x42532e9c`) and PPC (`0x4253172c`) look up the table cache,
search and parse the requested strings file (or create an empty strings
dictionary), then allocate and install the cache dictionary only if it was
absent. The target retains the parsed dictionary (or allocates the empty
dictionary), inserts it into the cache, and releases the temporary ownership.
The source previously created the cache before searching for the strings table,
re-read it after insertion, and omitted the matching temporary ownership
release. `NSBundle.m` now follows the target order and ownership flow. Static
paired IDA/source review with `git diff --check` only; no tests or builds were
run.

## `NSBundle _initInfoDictionary` initialization and file-manager order (2026-10-13)

default file manager after loading the candidate Info dictionary and installing

The source previously constructed the path and fetched the manager in local
initializers before setting the flag, and skipped the directory query if
dictionary allocation failed. `NSBundle.m` now follows the target call order
and performs the directory query independently of dictionary allocation.
Static paired IDA/source review with `git diff --check` only; no tests or

## `NSHTTPURLHandle` response-data callback flow (2026-10-13)

Compared `receivedDataBlock:forRequest:finished:` (PPC `0x425b5950`) and
`didLoadBytes:loadComplete:` (`0x425b60d8`) with `NSHTTPURLHandle.m`. While a
load is active, response blocks go to `didLoadBytes:`. Otherwise, error-page
blocks accumulate under the in-progress header key and move to the final error
page key on completion; header dictionaries and temporary data follow the same
copy/release order as IDA. Redirected loads forward available data to clients
and signal superclass completion with nil data; ordinary loads pass data and
completion through. Source matches these paths. Static PPC IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSHTTPURLHandle` request lifecycle (2026-10-13)

Compared `loadInForeground` (PPC `0x425b5410`), `beginLoadInBackground`
(`0x425b5610`), and `endLoadInBackground` (`0x425b57ac`) with
`NSHTTPURLHandle.m`. Foreground loading reuses or creates the host connection,
sends a GET request synchronously, releases the request before examining the
status, follows 3xx redirects, and returns nil for status 400 or above.
Background loading delegates to an existing redirect, reuses an active
connection, or creates a connection and enqueues a GET request; connection
failure reports the localized host error. Ending a redirected load delegates
to the redirect, while ending a direct load cancels the URL fetch, releases the
connection, and clears the ivar. Source matches both paths and their call
order. Static PPC IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSHTTPURLHandle` property lookup and response headers (2026-10-13)

Compared `propertyForKey:` (PPC `0x425b4fc8`),
`propertyForKeyIfAvailable:` (`0x425b529c`), and
`receivedHeaders:forRequest:` (`0x425b5bb8`) with `NSHTTPURLHandle.m`.
Property lookup returns available cached values after loading has started;
otherwise it performs a synchronous GET, releases the request before handling
the status, and either returns a lowercased header value or follows a redirect.
Available lookup delegates through a redirect and exposes redirection headers
only when cached headers exist. Response handling replaces existing cached
headers on 2xx/3xx responses, starts a redirected load or reports a loop,
reports 4xx/5xx failures, and logs and cancels requests for unknown status
codes; non-2xx paths release and clear
the connection. Source matches these branches and their cleanup order. Static
PPC IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

divergence, not a claim of timer-firing parity for nil mode lists.

receiver's zone before releasing the data. `addCharactersInRange:` checks the
mutation flag, then sets each bit in the requested range. Source matches the
allocation zone, release order, and loop bounds on both targets. Both
character-set maps validate and map all five methods. Static paired IDA/source-
map review only; no tests or builds were run.

The paired control flow also preserves the 21-to-29-second interval: after the
inner retry exits at 21 seconds, the under-30-second outer check returns
success without calling `breakLock` or retrying `tryLock`.

a `UserDefaults` subdirectory beneath that parent. The source then checked the
sentinel under the parent and acquired the lock after checking the sentinel
and data file. These caller differences were corrected in the later

## Foundation condition wait helpers versus Libc cthreads source (2026-10-14)

At the first review pass, the unmapped called helpers in the Foundation lock path were cthreads queue routines, not missing NSLock methods. IDA resolves `condition_wait_timeout` (i386 `0x42519558`, 506 bytes; PPC `0x4259d714`, 560), signal (i386 `0x42503410`, 85; PPC `0x4259d694`, 128), broadcast (i386 `0x42585c94`, 32; PPC `0x4259d654`, 64), `cproc_continue_timeout` (i386 `0x425380b4`, 124; PPC `0x4259d944`, 156), and `dequeue_unlock_send` (i386 `0x42585d2c`, 69; PPC `0x4259da70`, 108). Their callers are NSLock/NSCondition methods or the adjacent queue helpers. The closest repository implementations are `src/Libc-1/threads.subproj/cprocs.c:443-569`. The queue state transitions and message flow match, but they are not exact source-body mappings: the Foundation timeout helper receives seconds and converts to milliseconds before `msg_receive`, while Libc `condition_wait_timeout` accepts milliseconds directly; Foundation's timeout error paths raise `NSException`, while Libc logs/asserts/aborts. NSLock.m preserves the same duration by converting its remaining seconds to milliseconds before calling the Libc API. These platform helper bodies were outside the Foundation source maps at that review point; the later “Foundation cthreads timeout helper reconstruction” entry records their implementation and mappings. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.


Re-decompiled all five helpers in the live i386 and PPC databases. Both
`condition_wait_timeout` bodies convert their double-seconds argument to a
millisecond receive timeout, enqueue the current cproc as blocked, release the
condition spin lock and caller mutex, and receive a 24-byte message. Interrupted
receives retry. On timeout, they recheck whether a signaler already marked the
thread `CPROC_EATING`; otherwise they remove that cproc from the wait queue,
preserve the other queue entries, and return the timeout result after restoring
the running state. A successful receive restores the running state and returns
the signaled result. Both variants then reacquire the caller mutex. Signal
removes one waiter and broadcast drains the queue recursively; each selected
waiter is marked `CPROC_EATING` before its 24-byte wake message is sent. The
send helper accepts success and `SEND_TIMED_OUT`; other send or receive errors
raise `NSException` in Foundation. The generic Libc helpers retain their
millisecond argument and aborting diagnostics. This confirms the reconstruction
must own the timeout unit and error path inside Foundation while preserving the
shared cproc queue protocol. No source behavior changed; static paired IDA/source
review only, no tests or builds were run.

The timeout conversion is `seconds * 1000`, truncated toward zero, with
`UINT_MAX` used when the product is greater than or equal to `UINT_MAX`; the
unbounded `1.0e20` caller value therefore also reaches `msg_receive` as
`UINT_MAX`. Raw paired pseudocode confirms this conversion on both targets.

The target error format strings are also present in both images:
`*** condition_wait_timeout(): msg_receive failure with exit code %d` and
`*** condition_signal_timeout(): msg_end failure with exit code %d` on i386;
they are at `0x425fdb6e` and `0x425fdbb2`, respectively. PPC adds a trailing
underscore to each helper name in the strings at `0x426209cc` and `0x42620a14`.
The send error raised from `cproc_continue_timeout` uses the signal helper's
message.

Re-decompiled the five timed lock callers on both architectures as well. Their
IDA bodies pass the remaining interval in seconds directly to
`condition_wait_timeout` (`-waitUntilDate:` passes `timeIntervalSinceNow`; the
date-based lock methods pass their computed interval). At that review point,
source multiplied those intervals by 1000 before calling Libc's millisecond
API. The call-boundary difference is closed by the later “Foundation cthreads
timeout helper reconstruction” entry.

## NSDistributedLock state and ownership parity (2026-10-14)

Reviewed the remaining `NSDistributedLock` methods in both IDA targets against
`NSDistributedLock.m`: `lockWithPath:`, `initWithPath:`, `tryLock`, `unlock`,
`breakLock`, `lockDate`, `dealloc`, and `description`. The factory allocates,
initializes, and autoreleases; path initialization checks directory creation,
allocates the private state in the receiver's zone, and initializes its guard,
copied path, and ownership flag. Lock acquisition serializes local state,
creates the directory, returns false for an existing lock or unrepresentable
path, and raises for other `mkdir` failures. Unlock forwards to `breakLock`;
`breakLock` removes the lock directory and clears ownership under the guard.
`dealloc` acquires the guard, conditionally removes a held lock directory,
releases the path and guard, and frees the private state. `lockDate` converts
the path modification time to a date, while
`description` reports class, receiver, lock state, and path. Existing paired
source-map entries cover these methods on i386 and PPC. No source behavior or
mapping changed. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were
run.

## NSMachPort retain and release state-machine parity (2026-10-15)

Compared retain, release, and retainCount in i386 IDA (0x42526b70,
0x4250de38, 0x4258007c) and PPC IDA (0x42514418, 0x4250f28c, 0x42595230)
with NSPort.m. i386 stores the count in bits 8 through 31 and flags in the
low byte; PPC stores the count in the low 24 bits and flags in the high byte.
Both retain paths lock, increment, unlock, then report the retain event.
Both release paths report the release event before locking; a nonzero count
is decremented and unlocked, while a first final release marks the port,
removes it from the table, unlocks, invalidates, and deallocates if the count
remains zero. On a repeated release while already marked, both binaries unlock
and call dealloc without rechecking the count. Source follows these branches.
`retainCount` returns the packed count plus one. No source correction is
indicated. Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

bytes) and i386 IDA (`0x42588430`, 104 bytes) with `NSCharacterSet.m:1812`.
PPC allocates the concrete mutable set, decodes the property list, then
initializes the set with that bitmap. i386 decodes first, allocates the
concrete set, then initializes it. The i386 pseudocode omitted the bitmap
argument, but disassembly shows the decoded result saved on the stack across
allocation and supplied to `initWithBitmapRepresentation:`. Both targets then
deallocate the original receiver and return the concrete set. Source preserves
the PPC/i386 order split and replacement ownership path. Static paired
IDA/source/disassembly review only; no tests or builds were run.
## `NSMutableCharacterSet` allocation and copy parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `+[NSMutableCharacterSet allocWithZone:]` (PPC `0x4254b494`, 144
bytes; i386 `0x42587084`, 117 bytes), `copyWithZone:` (PPC `0x425a3428`,
72 bytes; i386 `0x4258b098`, 59 bytes), and `mutableCopyWithZone:` (PPC
`0x425a3594`, 96 bytes; i386 `0x4258b1a0`, 63 bytes) with
`NSCharacterSet.m`. Both allocation methods redirect allocation of the base
class to `NSConcreteMutableCharacterSet` and delegate subclass allocation to
the superclass. Copying requests a mutable copy, makes it immutable, then
returns it. The abstract mutable-copy method logs and raises
`doesNotRecognizeSelector:`. Source matches both target paths. Static paired
IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.
## `NSCharacterSet` bitmap, count, and emptiness parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `bitmapRepresentation` (PPC `0x425a047c`, 240 bytes; i386
`0x42588260`, 199 bytes), `count` (PPC `0x425a0600`, 72 bytes; i386
`0x42588388`, 61 bytes), and `isEmpty` (PPC `0x425a075c`, 156 bytes; i386
`0x42588498`, 121 bytes) with `NSCharacterSet.m`. Both bitmap methods allocate
8,192 bytes, zero the buffer, and query membership for U+0000 through U+FFFE;
PPC uses `initWithLength:` and i386 uses `initWithCapacity:`. Both count
methods pass the bitmap bytes and 8,192-byte length to
`_countMembersOfBitmap`. Emptiness returns YES for nil data and otherwise
scans the data's length for a nonzero byte. Source matches both targets.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.
## `NSPerformTimer newPerformSelector:` cache and initialization parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `+[NSPerformTimer newPerformSelector:target:argument:order:modes:]`
in PPC IDA (`0x4251d78c`, 428 bytes) and i386 IDA (`0x425165d4`, 294 bytes)
with `NSPerformTimer.m`. Both targets lock the optional cache lock, remove the
first available object from the four-slot cache, then unlock. Reused objects
report allocation when statistics are enabled; a cache miss allocates a new
object. Both store target, selector, argument, and order, clear the invalid
bit, copy the modes into the object, and return it retained. Source matches
both paths and target-specific flag layout. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.
## `NSPerformTimer` release and cache teardown parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `release` (PPC `0x4251eec4`, 80 bytes; i386 `0x425123fc`, 44
bytes) and `dealloc` (PPC `0x4251ed1c`, 424 bytes; i386 `0x42516dc0`,
328 bytes) with `NSPerformTimer.m`. Both release methods decrement the stored
reference count when nonzero and call `dealloc` at zero. Deallocation first
invalidates the performer, then inserts it into the first empty cache slot
under the optional lock. A cached performer has its target, selector,
argument, order, modes, link, firing flag, filler, and reference count reset;
the invalid flag remains set until constructor reuse clears it. Reused objects
report deallocation when statistics are enabled. When the four-slot cache is
full, both targets unlock and call superclass deallocation. Source matches
the PPC and i386 field layouts and lifecycle. Static paired IDA/source review
only; no tests or builds were run.
## `NSPerformTimer fire` selector logging argument (2026-10-15)

Compared `-[NSPerformTimer fire]` in PPC IDA (`0x4251fcd0`, 236 bytes) and

## Foundation source-map semantic revalidation (2026-10-15)

Revalidated all 108 Foundation `source-map.json` files against the current
repository with `binrecon.schema.load_source_map(..., repo_root=...)`. All maps
passed schema and semantic source-path/source-line validation, including the
four port and port-coder maps added since the previous 104-map review. This
checks map structure and source locations, not binary behavior or build
parity. Then matched each map's `reference_sha256` to the live IDA database and
checked every mapped function's start address, name, and size: all 4,205 PPC
records in 57 maps and all 4,090 i386 records in 51 maps matched with zero
errors. These checks validate map metadata and function boundaries, not source
body equivalence. No tests or builds were run.

## `NSMapTable` key/value array extraction parity (2026-10-15)

prototype. Source matches both paths. Static paired IDA/source/disassembly
review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSMapTable` mutation and callback parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `NSMapInsert`, `NSMapInsertKnownAbsent`, `NSMapInsertIfAbsent`,
and `NSMapRemove` in PPC IDA (`0x425016f4`, `0x425094bc`, `0x42525930`,
`0x4250aa94`) and i386 IDA (`0x4250489c`, `0x4251301c`, `0x425293cc`,
`0x4250dd88`) with `NSMapTable.m:312-363`. Both targets reject the reserved
key, hash it before insertion, retain values before replace-mode insertion,
release the replaced value on replacement, and retain the key after successful
insertion. The absent-only variants retain key and value only after success;
`NSMapInsertKnownAbsent` describes and raises for an existing key, while
`NSMapInsertIfAbsent` returns the existing key. Removal skips an empty table
and, after a successful delete, releases key before value. Source's shared
insertion helper and wrappers preserve these branches and callback order.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

Compared `NSCreateMapTableWithZone`, `NSCreateMapTable`, `NSFreeMapTable`,

`0x42546198`) with `NSMapTable.m:196-231`. Both constructors allocate a
0x28-byte table in the requested or null zone, create its simple dictionary
with the requested capacity/equality callback/zone, and store both callback

Static paired IDA/source/disassembly review only; no tests or builds were run.

## `NSCopyMapTableWithZone` retain-callback receiver divergence (2026-10-15)

Paired pseudocode and raw disassembly for PPC (`0x4256d474`, 340 bytes) and
i386 (`0x42563054`, 258 bytes) show that after a successful copied-table
insertion, each target checks the copied table's retain-callback slot for
non-null, then loads and calls the callback pointer from the original table's
corresponding slot (offsets `0x0c` for keys and `0x1c` for values). Source at
`NSMapTable.m` now checks the copied table's retain-callback slot, loads the
callback pointer from the original table, and invokes it with the copy as its
context, matching both targets. The callback pointers start equal, but can
differ if a retain callback mutates the original table's callback record
during copying. Static paired IDA/source/disassembly review only; no tests or
builds were run.

## `NSValue` copy, description, and coding parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `copyWithZone:`, `description`, `encodeWithCoder:`, and
`initWithCoder:` in PPC IDA (`0x425c372c`, `0x425c37dc`, `0x42551048`,
`0x425c39ac`) and i386 IDA (`0x4259fc88`, `0x4259fd40`, `0x4259fdf4`,
`0x4259ffd4`) with `NSValue.m:545-601, 621-626`. Copy obtains the type and
size, uses stack storage through 1,024 bytes, creates a value in the requested
zone, and frees larger temporary buffers. Description uses the same payload
size and returns the data description; PPC allocates the data object before
asking for `objCType`, while i386 asks for the type first, matching the source
guards. Coding rejects `^v`, writes the type string then its bytes, and frees
large storage. Decoding saves the receiver's zone, deallocates the receiver,
and constructs a decoded value in that zone. Source matches both targets.
Static paired IDA/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## HashTable decoded capacity high-count shift parity (2026-10-15)

Refined the earlier `_exp2m1` capacity note after checking the target shift instructions. For decoded counts above `0x7fffffff`, `NSLog2(count) + 1` is 32. i386 `shl edx, cl` masks the shift count to five bits, so `_exp2m1` returns 0; PPC `slw` returns 0 for a shift of 32, so `_exp2m1` returns `0xffffffff`. `NSCompatibilityHashCapacity` now preserves its loop for ordinary counts and returns 0 for this i386-only upper range. PPC's loop already returns `0xffffffff`. Refreshed source-line anchors in the paired compatibility maps and the distant-object maps; the affected maps plus `i386-text-symbols` pass semantic validation. Static paired IDA/disassembly/source review only; no tests or builds were run.

Ambiguous and path-mismatched records were left unchanged. All 109 source maps passed schema and semantic validation, and the 6,696 mapped Objective-C records had no remaining unique same-path stale anchors. Static source-map audit only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSDistributedLock paired lifecycle parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `lockWithPath:`, `initWithPath:`, `tryLock`, `unlock`, `breakLock`, `lockDate`, `init`, `dealloc`, and `description` in both IDA targets with `NSDistributedLock.m`. Both initializers store a 12-byte private record in the receiver zone with an `NSLock`, a copied path, and an unlocked flag; failed directory validation releases the receiver and returns nil. `tryLock` serializes access with that guard, rejects an already-owned lock or an unrepresentable path, creates the directory with mode 0777, returns false for EEXIST, raises for other mkdir errors, and marks ownership only after success. `unlock` delegates to `breakLock`; that method removes the path and clears ownership while holding the guard. `lockDate` converts the filesystem modification timestamp into an NSDate. Deallocation holds the guard while removing an owned lock, releases the path and guard, frees the private record in its zone, and then calls super. The unsupported initializer raises with the current method name; `description` reports class, address, lock state, and path. Source follows both targets. Existing paired maps match function addresses, names, and sizes. Static paired IDA/source-map review only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSHTTPConnection response-header enrichment and body-length parity (2026-10-15)

Header enrichment sets the version from the text before the first space, parses the status between the first and second spaces, and stores the remaining reason text. With no second space, a three-character status above 99 is stored and returned without adding a reason key; malformed input receives status 599 and the localized `Bad header received from server` reason. Body sizing returns zero for HEAD, 1xx, 204, and 304 responses; otherwise it uses a nonempty content-length value or the `0x7fffffff` streaming sentinel. ## NSHTTPConnection synchronous result callbacks and port recovery parity (2026-10-15)

Compared PPC `receivedHeaders:forRequest:` (`0x425b1b80`), `receivedDataBlock:forRequest:finished:` (`0x425b1c64`), `connectionFailedDuringRequest:` (`0x425b1dd8`), `requestWasCancelled:` (`0x425b1e0c`), and `portBecameInvalid:` (`0x425b21bc`) with `NSHTTPConnection.m:335-401,471-490`. Header callbacks create a synchronous record, append it under `_lock`, then release the local ownership. Data callbacks ignore cancelled requests, append nonempty data to the record matching request identity, and unlock the condition only on completion. ## `NSUnarchiver -decodeValueOfObjCType:at:` parity (2026-10-15)

Compared `-[NSUnarchiver decodeValueOfObjCType:at:]` in i386 IDA (`0x425122d0`, 99 bytes) and PPC IDA (`0x4250cda0`, 124 bytes) with `NSArchiver.m:1366-1376`. Both targets decode the encoded type string, check it against the requested type, decode the value, and report an excess descriptor character when the decoder returns a non-terminator. The source passes a local `NSUnarchiverContext` to its internal helpers; those helpers receive the unarchiver directly in both targets. In `__decodeObject` (i386 `0x42508a64`, 626 bytes; PPC `0x42502770`, 672 bytes), both targets read the current object zone from the unarchiver for `allocWithZone:`, while source uses `context->objectZone` at `NSArchiver.m:1083`. In `__decodeValueOfObjCType` (i386 `0x42507bc0`, 1,391 bytes; PPC `0x42501904`, 1,080 bytes), both targets read the live object-zone field when copying a decoded `*` string. i386 Hex-Rays leaves the switch indirect, but its `*` jump-table entry resolves to `0x42507eac`; decoded instructions at that branch load `[unarchiver + 0xc]` before the `NSZoneMalloc` call, matching the `objectZone` ivar offset in `NSArchiver.h`. Because `setObjectZone:` updates the unarchiver, an `initWithCoder:` callback can change the zone used for subsequent object allocations during recursive aggregate decoding; a following `*` field has the same stale-snapshot issue on both targets. The `decodeValuesOfObjCTypes:` (i386 `0x425058f0`, 82 bytes; PPC `0x425052e4`, 136 bytes) and `decodeArrayOfObjCType:count:at:` (i386 `0x42533904`, 471 bytes; PPC `0x425477f8`, 604 bytes) wrappers also reuse one context per public call in source while passing the unarchiver to each target helper call. Paired maps match both helper functions at source lines 1057 and 1136 and all three public method identities, addresses, sizes, and source anchors. Updating both `context->objectZone` reads in the helpers to use `unarchiver->objectZone` is pending design approval. Static paired IDA pseudocode/disassembly/source-map review only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSBundleLoadCode class-callback state ordering (2026-10-16)

Compared `_NSBundleLoadCode` in i386 IDA (`0x4250b3c8`, 1,368 bytes) and PPC IDA (`0x4259b204`, 1,148 bytes) with `NSBundleLoadCode` in `NSBundle.m:395-517`, and checked both `_NSBundleLoadCallback` bodies. The target bodies do not reset `_NSGlobalLoadingClassCount` before `objc_loadModules`; they clear the global class buffer and its count after loading. The callback appends each class to that shared buffer. Source previously set `NSBundleLoadingClassCount = 0` immediately before `objc_loadModules`; it now preserves the shared count through nested loads and retains the target-matching post-load cleanup. This is equivalent on the ordinary sequential path when the previous invocation completed its cleanup, but it changes the state seen by a nested load while an outer loader has accumulated callbacks. `objc4-1/runtime/objc-load.m:548-552` explicitly documents recursive `objc_loadModules` calls from load messages, confirming that re-entry is supported by the runtime; `objc_loadModule` reaches `NSLinkModule` at line 603 after setting the class callback. The removed pre-reset had discarded outer callback classes on re-entry. Source now matches both Foundation targets and preserves the accumulated callback list until the outer load finishes. Static paired IDA/runtime-source review only; no tests or builds were run.

## NSSimpleHashing dictionary and set construction parity (2026-10-16)

Compared `NSCreateSimpleDictionary` and `NSCreateSimpleSet` in i386 IDA (`0x42503a3c`, 117 bytes; `0x4250d3dc`, 104 bytes) and PPC IDA (`0x4250d638`, 200 bytes; `0x4251d6dc`, 176 bytes) with `NSSimpleHashing.m:128-139,359-392`. Boundary difference: when no capacity entry is large enough, both target loops advance to level 28 and use that index for the bucket-count lookup; the source helper instead clamps to level 27. The word read at index 28 differs by target: i386 reads `0x30000000` at `0x425a45a0`, while PPC reads zero at `0x425c9af8`. `NSConcreteMutableDictionary` and `NSConcreteDictionary initWithObjects:forKeys:count:` reject counts above `0x07ffffff`; `NSCountedSet` rejects values above `0x0fffffff`. However, `NSCreateMapTableWithZone` passes its capacity directly to `NSCreateSimpleDictionary` without a size check, so the boundary is reachable through the map-table API. The source still clamps to level 27. No code change was made because reproducing the target-specific level-28 allocation and initialization effects would intentionally recreate an out-of-range table read and potentially enormous or wrapping allocations. ## `deserializeAlignedBytesLengthAtCursor:` extended-header bounds divergence (2026-10-16)
